days.title: Arrival in Tokyo
days.tagline: Touch down at Narita. Neon lights and konbini runs await.
highlights: 18:30 — Land at Narita Airport
Narita Express to Shibuya — 75 min, ¥3,250
Buy Suica IC cards at the airport kiosk
Check into hotel. Light konbini dinner — onigiri is your new best friend
days.food: Konbini onigiri — umeboshi, kombu fillings are naturally GF + vegan. Available 24/7.
days.tip: Withdraw yen at 7-Eleven ATMs — best rates, English menus. Japan runs on cash.

days.title: TeamLab & Harajuku
days.tagline: Immersive digital art, then the sensory overload of Shibuya at night.
highlights: TeamLab Borderless at Azabudai Hills — ¥3,800, book 2 months ahead
Meiji Shrine — ancient forest in the heart of the city
Harajuku & Takeshita Street — pop culture, fashion, chaos
Shibuya Crossing at dusk — you live here. Golden Gai after dark.

activities.name: Dinner — Ain Soph Journey (vegan, GF options)

transport.note: All within central Tokyo, use Suica

days.food: Ain Soph Journey (Shinjuku) — fully vegan, GF options. Afuri ramen in Harajuku — ask for tamari.
days.tip: Wear dark clothing at TeamLab — projections look best on black. Book tickets the moment they open (2 months ahead).

days.title: Kamakura
days.tagline: 13th-century capital. Giant Buddha, ocean temples, island at sunset.
highlights: JR Yokosuka Line from Shibuya — 60 min, ¥940
Tsurugaoka Hachimangū shrine → Komachi-dōri street
Kōtoku-in — the Great Buddha, 13m tall, cast in 1252
Hase-dera Temple — ocean views, hydrangeas in May
Enoden train to Enoshima Island — caves, shrine, panoramic views
days.food: Bowls Kamakura (plant-based café near Hase). Look for vegetable tempura sets (note: batter has gluten).
days.tip: Time your visit to catch golden hour at Enoshima observation tower.

days.title: Mt Fuji
days.tagline: The iconic pagoda-and-peak view. Fuji is famously shy — go early.
highlights: Highway bus from Shibuya → Kawaguchiko — 2 hrs, ¥2,200
Chureito Pagoda — 398 steps to THE photo. Best light before noon.
Kawaguchiko Ropeway to Mt Tenjō — panoramic Fuji + lake view
Walk the north shore of Lake Kawaguchi — Fuji reflected in water
days.food: Limited veg/GF options around Kawaguchiko. Bring snacks from Tokyo. Rice dishes at lakeside restaurants.
days.tip: Clouds roll in by midday almost daily. The early bus is non-negotiable.

days.title: Tokyo → Kumamoto
days.tagline: Six hours south by bullet train. Welcome to Kyushu.
highlights: Shinkansen: Tokyo → Shin-Osaka (Hikari, 2h45) → Kumamoto (Sakura, 3h10)
Ekiben bento from Tokyo Station — an essential ritual
Kumamoto Castle — rebuilt after 2016 earthquake, stunning stone walls
Shimotori covered arcade — Kumamoto's beating heart
days.food: Ekiben bento from Tokyo Station — incredible selection. Ask for 'yasai no obentō' (vegetable bento).
days.tip: Window seat on the right side heading south for occasional Fuji glimpses early on.

days.title: Mt Aso & Bike Ride
days.tagline: Active volcano, vast caldera, then e-bikes through landscapes most tourists never see.
highlights: JR Hōhi Line → Aso Station — 75 min through mountains
Morning: Bokuya Rides guided e-bike through protected grasslands
Rolling hills, volcanic panoramas, thrilling downhill return
Afternoon: Nakadake Crater — steaming vents, turquoise lake (if accessible)
Kusasenri — vast green meadows inside the caldera
days.food: Limited veggie options in Aso area. Bring snacks from Kumamoto konbini. Rice-bowl restaurants for GF.
days.tip: Book Bokuya Rides at asocalderatourism.com. Start with the ride while legs are fresh. Helmets provided.

days.title: Kumamoto → Onomichi
days.tagline: Shinkansen north. A hillside port town of cats, temples, and sea views.
highlights: Kumamoto → Hakata → Fukuyama → Onomichi — 3.5 hrs total
Optional: 2-hr Hiroshima Peace Memorial detour en route
Senkoji Ropeway — hilltop park overlooking the Seto Inland Sea
Cat Alley (Neko no Hosomichi) — narrow paths with feline street art
Reserve bikes at Onomichi terminal for tomorrow's Shimanami Kaido
days.food: Onomichi ramen is the local specialty (not veggie-friendly). Try Komichi Café near Cat Alley for lighter fare.
days.tip: If you can spare 2 hrs, detour to Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park en route. It's one of the most powerful experiences in Japan.

days.title: Shimanami Kaido → Osaka
days.tagline: 70 km across 6 islands. Then straight to Japan's kitchen.
highlights: 06:30 — Send bags via takkyubin to Osaka hotel (~¥2,500/bag)
07:00 — Pick up e-bikes, ferry to Mukaishima
Ride across 6 islands — soaring bridges, Seto Inland Sea blue
Stop at Setoda, Omishima shrines, beaches along the way
~15:00 — Drop bikes at Imabari terminal
Imabari → Okayama → Shin-Osaka — train ~3.5 hrs. Arrive ~19:00.

activities.name: Send bags via takkyubin
activities.note: per bag, arrives next day at Osaka hotel

activities.name: Pick up e-bikes at Onomichi terminal
Arrive Osaka, check into Namba hotel

transport.note: Ride Onomichi → Imabari (70km), then train to Osaka

days.food: Pack snacks before starting. Setoda has Dolce gelato shop. Omishima has mikan everything. Konbini stops on islands.
days.tip: Takkyubin: drop bags at any konbini or Yamato office by morning. Follow the blue line on the road. E-bikes worth every yen.

days.title: Osaka — Dōtonbori & Shinsekai
days.tagline: Neon canals, retro towers, and the art of eating till you drop.
highlights: Sleep in — your legs deserve it after yesterday
Dōtonbori — the neon-lit canal, Glico Running Man sign
Shinsekai — retro district under Tsutenkaku Tower
Street food crawl — takoyaki, okonomiyaki, yakiimo
Hozenji Yokocho at dusk — stone-paved alley, tiny restaurants

activities.name: Late start — rest day for legs

days.food: Paprika Shokudo Vegan (Namba). Green Earth (Shinsaibashi). For GF okonomiyaki, ask 'kome-ko de dekimasu ka?' (rice flour?).
days.tip: Osaka's motto is kuidaore — eat till you drop. Dōtonbori at night is pure electricity.

days.title: Osaka — Castle & Markets
days.tagline: Castle parks, market stalls, and the city that never stops eating.
highlights: Osaka Castle — 8-story keep, panoramic city views, ¥600
Walk through Castle Park — beautiful in mid-May greenery
Kuromon Market — 'Osaka's Kitchen', browse 170+ stalls
Shinsaibashi arcade — covered shopping stretching for blocks
days.food: Kuromon Market — look for fresh fruit, pickles, rice dishes. Mochi (glutinous rice ≠ gluten!) is naturally GF.
days.tip: Kuromon Market before 2pm — stalls close early. Supermarket bento after 7pm is 30-50% off.

days.title: Kyoto
days.tagline: Thousands of torii gates. Gold temples. Bamboo forests. Geisha at dusk.
highlights: JR Special Rapid to Kyoto — 30 min, ¥580
Fushimi Inari — go before 9am. Thousands of vermillion gates.
Kinkaku-ji — gold-leaf temple reflected in mirror pond
Arashiyama Bamboo Grove → Tenryū-ji → Togetsukyo Bridge
Gion at dusk — traditional machiya, geiko quarter
days.food: Kyoto has the best vegan scene in Japan. Shigetsu at Tenryū-ji (shōjin ryōri, ¥3,300–5,500). Mumokuteki Café. Falafel Garden (Gion).
days.tip: Fushimi Inari at dawn is life-changing. The first tunnel of gates, almost empty, almost holy.

days.title: Nara Day Trip
days.tagline: Sacred deer, the world's largest wooden building, and deep calm.
highlights: JR or Kintetsu to Nara — 45 min from Osaka, ~¥800
Nara Park — 1,200 free-roaming sacred deer
Tōdai-ji — the Great Buddha Hall, world's largest wooden structure
Kasuga Taisha — shrine with 3,000 stone and bronze lanterns
Naramachi — traditional merchant quarter, craft shops, cafés
days.food: Naramachi has quiet cafés with set meals. Look for tofu-based dishes. Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) — veggie versions exist.
days.tip: The deer bow for shika senbei crackers — bow back! Watch your maps and tickets though, they'll eat paper.

days.title: Osaka → Tokyo
days.tagline: Final bullet train. Choose your Tokyo finale.
highlights: Morning: last Osaka stroll — pick up any remaining omiyage
Shinkansen Shin-Osaka → Tokyo — 2h45, ¥13,870
Option A: Asakusa — Sensō-ji, Tokyo's oldest temple
Option B: Akihabara — electronics, anime, retro gaming
Farewell dinner — Golden Gai or Michelin-star shōjin ryōri
days.food: Daigo near Shiba Park — 2-Michelin-star Buddhist vegan. Book ahead. Or casual Golden Gai.
days.tip: For a special last meal: Daigo is extraordinary. Otherwise, kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) — kappa, avocado, inari are veggie.

days.title: Departure
days.tagline: One last Tokyo morning. Then Narita. Then memories.
highlights: Tsukiji Outer Market — breakfast stalls, tamagoyaki, fresh fruit
Last shopping — Tokyo Station omiyage shops are incredible
Japanese Kit-Kats, matcha sweets, furoshiki wrapping cloths
19:00 — Narita Express to airport
22:50 — ✈️ Fly home to Warsaw. Sayonara, Japan.
days.food: Stock up on snacks at Narita — excellent selection. Senbei (rice crackers, GF!), mochi, regional KitKats.
days.tip: Tax-free shopping: ¥5,000+ at participating stores = ~10% savings. Don't open sealed items before leaving Japan.

japanesePhrases.meaning: I can't eat meat or fish
Do you have tamari soy sauce?

japanesePhrases.japanese: Dashi wa katsuobushi nashi de onegai shimasu
japanesePhrases.meaning: Please make dashi without bonito flakes

safeFoods: Onigiri (rice balls) — umeboshi, kombu, nattō fillings
Mochi — glutinous rice ≠ gluten, naturally GF
watchOut: Soy sauce (shōyu) contains wheat → request tamari
Dashi broth usually made with bonito (fish) → ask for kombu dashi
Miso soup often has bonito dashi

jrPassAnalysis.recommendation: Buy individual tickets. After the 2025 price increase, the 14-day pass (¥80,000) costs more than individual tickets (~¥65,000–70,000). You also get to ride the faster Nozomi Shinkansen, saving ~30 min per leg.
jrPassAnalysis.note: If you value convenience over savings, a 7-day pass activated Day 5 roughly breaks even.

transport.suicaCard: Buy at airport kiosk. ¥2,000 (¥500 deposit + ¥1,500 balance). Works on all metro, JR local, buses, konbini payments.

takkyubin.what: Luggage forwarding service — send bags between hotels
takkyubin.how: Drop at any konbini (7-Eleven, FamilyMart) or Yamato Transport office

bookings.note: At JR ticket counters (midori no madoguchi)

budget.note: Excludes flights. Mid-range estimates. 2 hotel rooms for 4 people.

packing: Light rain jacket — May has sudden showers
Layers — Mt Aso highlands are cooler
Small towel — many restrooms lack hand dryers
Allergy/dietary card in Japanese (print before trip)
Minimal luggage — lots of stairs and tight trains
Coin purse — Japan uses more coins than expected
